Alamance County by the numbers

How is property tax set up for a house seller in Alamance County?

A single county department handles listing, valuation and collection of taxes on everything taxable. The department is at 124 W. Elm St. in Graham, open weekdays from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., and its phone line is (336) 228-1312.

The county was formed in 1849 from part of Orange County and covers about 434 square miles. Graham is the seat and Burlington is the largest community. The towns of Elon, Haw River, Green Level, Ossipee, Swepsonville and Alamance, plus parts of Mebane and Gibsonville, fall inside the county. Textile mills along the Haw River drove its early growth.

Four things shape a sale here: the January 1 listing date, the September 1 due date, the 2027 revaluation, and a delinquent tax check at recording. Each gets its own section below.

What is the Alamance County property tax calendar?

Land Records explains that each parcel is listed to whoever owned it on January 1, and that date fixes the tax year. Statements go out in July, and the county charges no interest on a payment made by January 5.

Alamance County tax calendar and relief deadlines
DateWhat happens
January 1Listing date; owner on this day is billed
January 1 to 31Filing window for present-use and exemption applications
June 1Deadline for elderly, disabled, circuit breaker and disabled veteran relief
JulyBills mailed
September 1Bills due
January 5Last day to pay with no interest
January 6Delinquent; 2% interest added, then 0.75% on the sixth of each later month

A purchase that closes after January 1 can still produce a bill in the previous owner's name, even though the deed is recorded and the county has updated its record. Getting the mailing address corrected before July is the surest way to receive the bill on time.

Payment options are by mail (counted by postmark), in an indoor or outdoor drop box (credited as of the drop date), or online with a convenience fee. Registered vehicles are billed separately by the state through Tag and Tax Together at registration renewal.

What is happening with the 2027 revaluation in Alamance County?

Alamance County is revaluing every parcel effective January 1, 2027, and notices of value are scheduled to be mailed February 15, 2027. The last revaluation took effect January 1, 2023. North Carolina requires reappraisal at least every eight years under G.S. 105-286, and the county has chosen a four-year cycle.

Vincent Valuations, which assisted with the 2023 work, is performing the 2027 appraisal. Staff spend roughly two years in the field checking property features, comparing sales, and noting improvements. The county says its goal is to reach, or come close to, 100% of market value at revaluation.

A bigger number on the notice need not produce a bigger bill. County staff say rates fall as values rise, and a revenue neutral rate would keep the typical owner near last year's payment. Parcels that gained more than the average pay more, while laggards pay less.

If you plan to sell in 2027, open the notice the day it arrives. Your appeal period runs from its date, and late filings are generally turned away. The revaluation hotline is the same number as the tax department, (336) 228-1312.

How do I appeal a property value in Alamance County?

County appraisers hear informal reviews first. If that does not settle things, the matter moves to the Board of Equalization and Review. Filing windows differ by property type.

  • Real property: during the annual listing period, with documentation such as sales, photos, repair estimates or an appraisal.
  • Business and individual personal property: thirty days from the notice of value.
  • Registered vehicles: thirty days after the due date shown on the combined tag and tax notice.

The state outlines what comes next. The local board starts deliberating about the first week of April and allots each side a fixed time. A losing owner can go to the Property Tax Commission in Raleigh, a trial-style body that follows evidence rules and puts the burden on the taxpayer.

The county lists three typical grounds: a value above likely sale price, wrong square footage or condition on the record, and nearby sales pointing lower. It supplies a comparable sales tool and a property record search to help you gather proof.

What tax relief programs can Alamance County homeowners use?

June 1 is the usual filing deadline, and income caps change yearly, so get current figures from the tax department. An online eligibility calculator on the county site covers four of the programs.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: a seniors-and-disabled benefit that shelters the larger of $25,000 or half the home's taxable value, subject to an income cap.
  • Circuit breaker deferral: postpones part of the tax on a permanent residence, scaled to income. Eligible owners are 65 or older, or disabled, with five years of ownership and residence behind them.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: shelters the first $45,000 of assessed value for an honorably discharged veteran with a total, permanent service-connected disability, or for a surviving spouse. Age and income do not matter.
  • Present-use value: taxes qualifying farm, horticulture and forestry land on its use, but taxes deferred for the previous three years can be recaptured if the land leaves the program.

An owner who sells while a deferral or present-use status is in place should ask about payoff or recapture amounts before agreeing to a closing date.

What does Alamance County check about taxes when a deed is recorded?

The Register of Deeds states that every deed recorded after May 2, 2011, except timber deeds and releases, must go before the county Tax Department for delinquent tax certification first. That step follows G.S. 161-31(b). A seller with back taxes should plan to clear them so the certification can be issued.

After recording, the change reaches the property record through a short chain. The Register of Deeds keeps the document and gives it a book and page number. Land Records staff review it, change the owner name and mailing address, and push the update to the online record and GIS map. A simple sale of an existing parcel moves faster than a split or a new subdivision. If you do not see the change after several weeks, call Land Records with the book and page number.

If an owner has died, the county follows the estate file at the Clerk of Superior Court or recorded documents. Bills stay due on schedule meanwhile, and staff ask for the estate file number, the parcel number or address, and a mailing address.

Which housing figures stand out in Alamance County?

The 2020 count was 171,415 residents, and the July 2025 estimate of 186,177 is 8.6% above the 2020 base. Houses carry a $241,500 median value for 2020 to 2024, owners live in 65.0% of homes, and the county has 70,062 households. Median gross rent was $1,064 and median household income was $65,651.

Builders took out 2,027 permits in 2025. Poverty stood at 13.8%, and workers averaged 25.9 minutes of travel to work.

Look up your own parcel in the county property record search before you pick an asking price.

More questions about Alamance County, NC Property Tax Guide

When are Alamance County property taxes due?

They are due September 1. Interest does not start until January 6, so a bill paid by January 5 carries none. After that, 2% is added, plus 0.75% on the sixth of each following month.

Whose name is on the bill after an early-year purchase?

A bill can still arrive under the prior owner's name, because the county lists parcels to the January 1 owner. Divide the cost at closing and fix the mailing address before July.

When will new values from the 2027 revaluation arrive?

Notices of value are scheduled to be mailed February 15, 2027, for the January 1, 2027 effective date. Your appeal deadline is tied to the date on that notice.

What is the deadline for tax relief programs in Alamance County?

June 1 for the elderly or disabled exclusion, the circuit breaker deferral and the disabled veteran exclusion. Present-use and exemption filings fall in the January listing window.

Who do I call at Alamance County Tax Administration?

Call (336) 228-1312 or visit 124 W. Elm St. in Graham, weekdays from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. The same number handles revaluation questions.

Which Avery County office handles property tax?

The Avery County Tax Administrator's office, at 200 Montezuma Street in Newland, keeps the property records, sets assessments and bills the taxes. It runs two divisions: assessment at 828-733-8214 and collections at 828-733-8228.

Mail for the assessor goes to PO Box 305, Newland, NC 28657, and collection mail goes to PO Box 355 in the same town. The office hours quoted on the county's revaluation page are 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. An online lookup covers real estate, sales and tax bills, and a separate viewer shows tax maps.

One caution printed on the tax office page: the records and maps exist for valuation, and the legal description of a parcel is whatever the recorded deed says. Buyers and sellers should read the recorded deed instead of trusting a map line.

What is the Avery County tax rate?

For tax years 2023 through 2025 the county page prints a county rate of 0.335, a fire rate of 0.065 and a total of 0.40. The rate page shows no unit, so ask the tax office how to apply it to a bill.

Towns that levy their own tax add a separate municipal rate. The county publishes them with a code for each town, and those 2025 rates are in the table.

Avery County city tax codes and rates for 2025, as printed by the county tax office

01Banner Elk0.46

07Seven Devils0.47
08Sugar Mountain0.28

The county rate and the fire rate apply to every parcel, and the town rate applies where a town levies one, so ask the tax office which codes your parcel carries. Ten fire districts cover the county: Banner Elk, Crossnore, Elk Park, Fall Creek, Green Valley, Linville, Newland, Frank, Beech Mountain and Seven Devils.

When did Avery County last revalue property?

Values now in force were set as of January 1, 2022, and notices went out in March of that year. Counties must reappraise real property at least once in eight years, and Avery describes the goal as tax value that matches what a willing buyer and seller would agree on.

Avery did the work with its own staff instead of hiring an outside appraisal firm, and it says it took advice from outside sources on the schedule of values and on commercial property. The county's revaluation guide includes a sales ratio table. For houses it lists 344 sales at a 91 percent ratio in 2018, 430 sales at 83 percent in 2019, 699 sales at 71 percent in 2020 and 675 sales at 60 percent in 2021. A ratio of 100 percent would mean tax value equals sale price,, so the 60 percent figure for 2021 houses shows how far values had drifted from sale prices before the 2022 reset.

The same guide says a lower value does not follow from owning a house for decades. The statute requires uniform appraisal, so a long-held home is valued like comparable homes that sold recently.

How can an Avery County owner appeal a value?

First use the informal review named on the value notice, which is not an appeal. Use it to correct facts on your record, learn how the number was built and compare similar parcels. If you remain unhappy, ask in writing for a formal hearing.

Avery staffs its appeal board with appointed taxpaying citizens rather than commissioners, and that board sits between the first Monday of April and the first Monday of May. For the 2026 tax year its first meeting was Monday, April 13, requests had to arrive by final adjournment on Monday, May 4 at 3:00 p.m., and the county asked for appeal forms by April 28 so hearings could be scheduled. Sessions begin at 9:00 a.m. in courthouse Conference Room 106.

  • Pick up the application at the assessor's office or download it from the county site.
  • Bring record cards and sale prices for similar parcels nearby.
  • The question before the board is whether the value is accurate and fair. Ability to pay is outside its scope.

A further appeal goes to the Property Tax Commission, by notice within 30 days of the board's mailed decision.

What tax relief can Avery County homeowners claim?

The county lists three state programs plus a farm program, and a single owner gets only one of the first three. Pick up forms from the tax department and return them to the assessor by June 1.

  • Age 65 or disability exclusion: shelters the larger of $25,000 or half the appraised value of a permanent home, with income capped at $38,800 for 2026.
  • Circuit breaker deferment: limits the bill to 4 percent of income when income is at or under $38,800 and to 5 percent when it is at or under $58,200 (2026 figures). The excess is deferred and carried as a lien, and you reapply annually.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: removes up to $45,000 of appraised value without an age or income test; an unmarried surviving spouse may also qualify.
  • Present use value: farmers with active income from land can ask the office for a list of criteria and an application.

Deferred taxes matter in a sale. When a circuit breaker owner transfers the property, the last three years of deferred taxes come due with interest on the transfer date.

What does the Avery County listing period require?

Owners list taxable property during January, and the county says the duty is solely on the taxpayer even if a form never arrives. For 2026 the county asked for returns by March 2.

Items to list include untagged motor vehicles and motor homes, multi-year tagged trailers, improvements to real estate, income-producing personal property, business equipment, single-wide mobile homes, furnished rental property, and airplanes, boats and motors. Listing time is also when relief applications are taken.

State law gives the commissioners power to extend the period by up to 30 days in a non-revaluation year, and an individual with good cause can file a written request for more time before the regular period ends, though no extension runs past April 15.

How do Avery County taxes work when you sell?

Bills fall due September 1 and carry no interest until January 6, when 2 percent applies; after February 1 three-quarters of a percent accrues per month. Because the lien attaches on the listing date, an unpaid bill stays with the parcel through a sale.

Census data shows how big the stakes are: median owner-occupied value is $265,800, 83.0 percent of homes are owner-occupied and the county has 14,597 housing units against 6,791 households. With so many seasonal homes, bills often go to a second address, so make sure the tax office has a current mailing address. Get the exact balance from collections and hand it to the closing attorney so the bill is paid out of the proceeds.

More questions about Avery County, NC Property Tax Guide

How do I reach the Avery County tax office?

Assessment is 828-733-8214 and collections is 828-733-8228. Visit 200 Montezuma Street in Newland; the revaluation page gives hours as 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

What was the Avery County tax rate for 2025?

The county page prints 0.335 for county tax and 0.065 for fire tax, which totals 0.40. Towns add their own rate, from 0.28 in Sugar Mountain to 0.65 in Beech Mountain.

When is the Avery County revaluation?

The latest took effect January 1, 2022. The eight-year statutory limit means another one is due within that span, and the tax office page is where the schedule will appear.

How do I appeal my Avery County property value?

Ask the tax office for an informal review first, then file the written hearing application before the appeal board adjourns. In 2026 adjournment was May 4 at 3:00 p.m.

Can I get a break on Avery County property tax if I am 65 or disabled?

Yes, when income stays within the 2026 limit of $38,800. The exclusion shelters the larger of $25,000 or half the value, and the assessor must receive the form by June 1.

Davidson County by the numbers

Which Davidson County offices bill and value property?

Davidson County runs its property tax through a Tax Assessor side that lists and values property and a Tax Collector side that bills and collects. Both are found at 913 Greensboro Street, 3rd Floor, Suite 303, in Lexington (NC 27292), open weekdays from 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM. A second counter in Denton opens at 8:30 AM on weekdays.

  • Tax office and appeals line: 336-242-2160.
  • Collections line: 336-242-2180.
  • Mailing address for the assessor: P.O. Box 1617, Lexington, NC 27293.
  • Mailing address for payments: Davidson County Tax Collector, P.O. Box 1577, Lexington, NC 27293.

The county's Collections page says questions about listing, billing and assessed values go to the assessor's side, while the collector is responsible only for collecting what is owed.

What are the 2026 Davidson County tax rates?

The county's own line reads 0.5400 on the 2026 sheet, and a parcel inside a city, school district or fire district picks up that jurisdiction's line too. The sheet carries the word tentative in its heading, so verify the adopted numbers with the tax office.

Davidson County 2026 rate sheet, rates exactly as printed by the county
JurisdictionPrinted rate
County only0.5400
City of Lexington0.6500
City of Thomasville0.6200
Town of Denton0.6000
City of High Point0.7349
Town of Wallburg0.0500
Town of Midway0.0500
Lexington school0.1200
Thomasville school0.1900

Fire district rates are listed separately and run from 0.0965 for Reeds Fire to 0.1624 for Healing Springs Fire. City motor vehicle fees are $30.00 in Lexington and High Point, $20.00 in Thomasville and $5.00 in Denton, and the Lexington sheet notes that discounts are not applied to the city and municipal service district lines.

When are Davidson County property tax bills due?

Bills for land, buildings and business or personal items are mailed each July. They fall due September 1 and carry no interest until after January 5. A weekend January 5 pushes the deadline to the following business day.

The county gives a 1 1/2 percent discount for payment in July and a 1 percent discount in August. A January 5 postmark counts as timely, though the county advises mailing a full week early. Past-due real estate accounts are charged 2 percent for January and an extra 3/4 percent each month after that, which matches the state schedule. Payment plans have to be arranged when the annual bill arrives and finished by the delinquent date, and card payments are taken at the office.

What is happening with the Davidson County revaluation?

Davidson County's last revaluation took effect January 1, 2021, and the county's pages say the planned 2026 revaluation was postponed until 2027 under new legislation. State law requires counties to reappraise at least once every eight years, and the county reviews more than 97,000 parcels in a revaluation.

The county explains that revaluation is meant to equalize values, not raise revenue, and that tax rates are set by elected officials in June. Owners who appealed their 2026 or 2027 values on time do not need to refile, and any change from those appeals will apply to the 2027 tax year. The informal appeal deadline for the 2026 round was 5:00 PM on Thursday, April 30, 2026, and it has passed. The county's appeal page offers separate forms for the current 2026 value and the 2027 revaluation value, and the revaluation help address is revalhelp@davidsoncountync.gov.

What steps does a Davidson County owner follow to contest a value?

Appeals have three levels, and the first is an informal review with a county appraiser, who looks at your property record and any supporting evidence with you. If an error turns up, it can be fixed without a formal appeal.

The second step is a formal hearing at the county's Board of Equalization and Review. Under state law the commissioners sit as that board unless a special one is created; Davidson County describes its board as local residents with real estate knowledge, appointed by the commissioners. A written notice to the state Property Tax Commission is the step after an unwelcome board decision. The county lists reasons that do not count as grounds:

  • The size of the percentage increase or decrease.
  • A market value above the insurance value.
  • A feeling that the value is simply too high.
  • An owner's inability to pay the tax.

Which property tax relief programs can a Davidson County owner use?

State law sets up three homestead programs and lets each owner use just one. The first program, for older or disabled owners, excludes whichever is bigger: $25,000 or half the appraised value. Qualifying means being 65 or older, or disabled for good, and earning no more than $38,800 for 2026.

The circuit breaker is the second: it holds the bill to 4.0 percent of income for owners at or below the limit, and to 5.0 percent for owners whose income reaches 150 percent of it ($58,200 for 2026). Five years of owning and occupying the home come first. The third takes $45,000 off the value for a disabled veteran with no age or income test. Form AV-9 goes to the county assessor, and the county's property information page links to the homestead application. Any tax deferred under the circuit breaker turns into a lien and becomes payable when the property transfers, which matters at a sale.

What happens to unpaid Davidson County property tax?

Interest starts on a bill after the January 5 deadline, and after that the bill is subject to collection actions. The collector lists wage garnishment, attachment of bank accounts or rents, levy on personal property and, for real estate, tax foreclosure by sale at public auction.

  • Unpaid real estate accounts can be advertised in local newspapers from March 1 to June 30, at added cost to the taxpayer.
  • The county also lists sheriff's warrants, in rem foreclosures and attachment of the state tax refund.
  • State law sets the lien date as the listing date, so the lien exists before the bill is due.

The county posts a PDF list of 2025 delinquent taxpayers and a tax foreclosure list. If a sale is pending, Davidson County also requires a tax certificate before the Register of Deeds takes a deed, so a delinquent balance has to be cleared first.

What does the Census count in Davidson County?

The Census estimate for July 2025 is 180,182 residents, and the five-year survey counts 69,846 households, 74.4 percent of them owning. The median owned home is valued at $219,100. Monthly costs for owners carrying a mortgage come to $1,355 at the median, and the median household brings in $64,172 (2024 dollars).

The county's rate sheet lists Lexington, Thomasville, Denton, Wallburg, Midway and High Point as taxing cities and towns, along with two school districts and dozens of fire districts. Ask the tax office which of those lines apply to your parcel.

How should I handle taxes when I sell a Davidson County house?

Ask whether the seller's share of the current bill is prorated at closing, and if you want zero exposure, have the closing attorney pay the collector from the proceeds. Per the county, selling during the year does not release the January 1 owner from that year's bill.

Request a tax certificate early if no attorney is closing. Check the 2026 or 2027 appeal status too, because a value change from an appeal lands in the 2027 tax year.

Payment is due September 1, with no interest through January 5. July payments earn a 1 1/2 percent discount and August payments earn 1 percent.

Was the Davidson County revaluation postponed?

Yes. The county says its 2026 revaluation was postponed until 2027 under new legislation. Appeals filed on time for 2026 or 2027 values still get reviewed, and any change applies to the 2027 tax year.

How can I contest my Davidson County property value?

Start by filing the county's form for an informal sit-down with an appraiser. Only if that falls short does the matter go on to a formal hearing. The state Property Tax Commission hears later appeals, and the 30 days run from the board's mailing date.

What interest applies to late Davidson County taxes?

Past-due real estate accounts are charged 2 percent for January and 3/4 percent for each month after that. The county urges mailing payments at least five business days before the January 5 deadline.
